0.heading: Subscribe for Symbiotec Pharmalab Ltd IPO; Geojit Financial Services
0.intro: Geojit Financial Services, has come out with its report on Symbiotec Pharmalab Ltd The research firm has recommended to “ Subscribe” the ipo in its research report as on August 24, 2026.
0.body:
Geojit Financial Services, Symbiotec Pharmalab Ltd
Symbiotec Pharmalab Limited is a research and development-driven, sciencebased pharmaceutical and biotechnology company with capabilities across organic chemistry, biotechnology and complex injectables. The Company has over 30 years of industry experience and has evolved from a lab-scale steroidal-hormone API manufacturer into an industrial-scale, backward-integrated platform. It operates as both an API manufacturer and a contract development and manufacturing organisation (CDMO), while also expanding into complex injectables. Symbiotec has a strong global position in corticosteroid and steroidal-hormone APIs, with 38.2% and 23.8% global volume market share, respectively, in FY26. It is the only Indian and global player present across the top 10 APIs in both segments. Its portfolio of 60+ APIs caters to critical therapeutic areas including respiratory, dermatology, oncology and gynaecology.

Valuation and Outlook
At the upper price band of ₹988, the issue is valued at a P/E multiple of about 57.81x on its FY26 post-IPO EPS of ₹17.09. We give a 'SUBSCRIBE' rating to the issue for the following reasons.

1.headline: Atomberg IPO investors will inherit Rs 190 crore deferred bonus bill for founders
1.heading: Atomberg IPO investors will inherit Rs 190 crore deferred bonus bill for founders
1.intro: The amount is equivalent to 88 percent of the company’s total cash and bank deposits.
1.body:
Investors buying shares in Atomberg Technologies’ proposed initial public offering will inherit a Rs 190 crore liability owed by the consumer appliances company to its founders, Manoj Kumar Meena and Sibabrata Das, towards deferred bonuses awarded in earlier financial years.

The liability is significant when compared with Atomberg’s total cash and bank deposits, which stood at Rs 215.87 crore. The deferred founder bonus is equivalent to around 88 percent of this amount.

The company also recorded negative operating cash flow of Rs 218.98 crore in FY26 and it reported a loss of Rs 148.88 crore.

Atomberg’s draft red hearing prospectus (DRHP) and other historical financial statements reviewed by Moneycontrol show that the outstanding amount comprises bonuses awarded across two years. Meena and Das were awarded a combined Rs 59.57 crore in FY23 and another Rs 132.89 crore in FY24, taking the cumulative founder bonus to Rs 192.46 crore.

The unpaid deferred bonus liabilities stood at Rs 190.09 crore as of March 2026.

However, Atomberg’s draft red herring prospectus does not disclose the performance criteria or milestones used to determine bonuses of this magnitude. It also does not explain why the awards were structured as deferred bonuses.

More importantly for prospective investors, the offer document does not specify a payment date, instalment schedule or settlement trigger. The DRHP only says that the management bonus was “structured as a deferred bonus payable in future periods”.

The DRHP also does not state if the proceeds from the IPO will be used to pay the founder bonuses.

Atomberg plans to raise up to Rs 450 crore through a fresh issue, including Rs 90 crore for debt repayment, Rs 150 crore for brand-building and performance marketing, and Rs 100 crore for research and development.

To be sure, the remaining fresh proceeds which are categorised under general corporate purposes, a discretionary portion of the fundraise, can be used for this purpose, although the DRHP doesn't explicitly state such a use of the proceeds.

Nevertheless, the bonus remains a company liability and its eventual settlement will reduce cash available to the business after listing.

An email sent to Atomberg did not elicit a response till the time of publication.

Also Read: Atomberg IPO decoded: Issue size, investor exits, financials and key risks

A person privy to the developments, speaking on the condition of anonymity, told Moneycontrol that as disclosed in the company's DRHP, the management bonus represents a historical remuneration liability that has already been recognised in the company’s financial statements and was structured as a deferred bonus payable in future periods.

The founders hold a combined 27.75 percent of Atomberg on a fully diluted basis. The active ESOP schemes disclosed in the DRHP do not show any outstanding options or fresh grants to either founder.

Apart from these bonuses to be paid in the future, the DRHP shows that Manoj Kumar Meena and Sibabrata Das have received gross consideration of approximately Rs 71.57 crore from secondary share sales since 2019.

Meena received an estimated Rs 40.18 crore, while Das received Rs 31.39 crore, through sales to investors including A91 Emerging Fund, Jungle Ventures’ JV4, Steadview Capital, V-Sciences Investments and other buyers.

Atomberg’s revenue from operations increased 34.8 percent to Rs 1,293.77 crore in FY26 from Rs 959.51 crore in FY25. However, its loss widened 26.8 percent to Rs 148.88 crore from Rs 117.41 crore during the same period.

Atomberg began by selling energy-efficient brushless direct current, or BLDC, ceiling fans and has since expanded into other consumer appliance categories. Its portfolio now includes ceiling, pedestal, wall and exhaust fans, mixer grinders, water purifiers, cold-pressed juicers and smart locks, among other products sold under the Atomberg brand.
1.ai_impact_text_summary_s: Atomberg IPO investors face a Rs 190 cr deferred bonus liability to founders, nearly matching cash reserves. The DRHP lacks details, raising concerns given the company's negative cash flow and losses.

2.headline: Zetwerk starts investor roadshows, targets IPO launch by September-end
2.heading: Zetwerk starts investor roadshows, targets IPO launch by September-end
2.intro: The offering comprises a fresh issue of up to Rs 2,600 crore and an offer for sale of 9.68 crore shares by its founders and investors
2.body:
Peak XV and Accel-backed Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses Limited has started investor roadshows for its initial public offering (IPO) and is targeting a launch by the end of September, according to people aware of the plans.

While September-end is the earliest timeline for the launch that the company is targeting, sources added that the offering would likely be launched close to mid-October, depending on the progress of the roadshows and prevailing market conditions.

An email sent to Zetwerk did not elicit a response till the time of publication.

The Bengaluru-headquartered company’s offer comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to Rs 2,600 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 9.68 crore shares, according to its updated draft red herring prospectus filed on August 13.

Zetwerk plans to use Rs 1,250 crore from the fresh issue to repay company's borrowings and another Rs 550 crore to repay debt of nine subsidiaries. The remaining proceeds will be used for unidentified acquisitions, other strategic investments and general corporate purposes.

Founded in 2017 by Amrit Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan, Zetwerk describes itself as a technology-led, asset-light manufacturing platform. It aggregates manufacturing capacity across third-party suppliers and its own facilities through its proprietary Zetwerk OS platform.

The company serves industries including renewable energy, consumer electronics, artificial intelligence infrastructure, aerospace, defence, oil and gas, and industrial automation. As of March 2026, it had 6,979 suppliers in 26 countries and 26 owned manufacturing facilities in four countries.

Revenue from operations rose 40 percent to Rs 15,913.32 crore in FY26 from the previous year. Its restated total loss, however, widened to Rs 1,606.17 crore from Rs 370.71 crore. The FY26 loss included non-cash exceptional charges related to share-conversion adjustments and an impairment in its discontinued civil infrastructure business.

The largest OFS component comprises 2.30 crore shares offered by promoter-group entity Creovate Innovation. Founders Acharya and Ramakkrushnan will sell up to 1.42 crore shares each. Peak XV, Accel, Lightspeed and Kae Capital are among the other selling investors.

On a fully diluted basis, Peak XV Partners Investments V is the largest individual shareholder vehicle with a 9.12 percent stake, followed by Greenoaks Capital Opportunities Fund II at 8.61 percent, Ramakkrushnan at 8.36 percent, Accel India V at 7.74 percent and Acharya at 7.53 percent.
2.ai_impact_text_summary_s: Peak XV and Accel-backed Zetwerk Manufacturing plans an IPO by late September/mid-October. The offering includes a Rs 2,600 crore fresh issue and 9.68 crore share OFS. Proceeds will repay debt and fund acquisitions. While revenue rose, the company's losses widened in FY26.
